title: Max Skill Station Series #1 - #3
description: Ice Hockey Systems skill station series using a tire or cone, a short barrier, and a small net. The three versions progress through tight control turns, puck retrievals, single shifts, backwards-to-forwards transitions, and quick shooting.
coaching_points: Version 1: tight control turn, retrieve the puck from the barrier, pull it into the body, and shoot quickly.
Version 2: control the puck through a tight turn, single-shift around the barrier, protect it, and finish with a shot.
Version 3: start backwards, retrieve a puck around the tire, transition forward, single-shift to the backhand side, and shoot.
Keep the head over the puck during the shooting motion and repeat both directions.

title: Half Ice Side By Side Skills Series #1
description: Ice Hockey Systems half-ice skill series with four related progressions: control turns with a puck, backwards puck control, inside-out full circles, and inside-out forward-facing transitions. The versions stay grouped under one drill.
coaching_points: Control Turns: lead with the inside leg and upper body while using the outside edge of the inside leg.
Backwards with Puck: maintain posture, keep the blade closed, and initiate the turn with a C-cut.
Full Circles: stay in a strong hockey position and rotate the chest into the turn.
Inside-Out Facing Forward: stay on the balls of the feet through forward/backward transitions and keep the head up.

title: Circle Stickhandling Series
description: Ice Hockey Systems stickhandling station with three progressions inside a faceoff circle. Players work creativity and control, then reaction to a moving partner, then puck control combined with passing to players outside the circle.
coaching_points: Progression 1: be creative through the objects while staying in full control and aware of traffic.
Progression 2: follow a moving partner while keeping the head up and maintaining puck control.
Progression 3: move through the objects while identifying and passing to open players outside the circle.
Keep repetitions short and active so players maintain pace and awareness.
